title: One Person, One Verb: Purpose with the Infinitive

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the rule of B2 Unit 4: when the same person acts in both parts of the sentence, Spanish uses an infinitive, and when the second action belongs to someone else it uses *que* + subjunctive. Purpose follows the same rule. You know *para* + infinitive from A2 Unit 30 and *con el fin de* + infinitive from B1 Unit 32: *Estudio para aprobar* means "I study in order to pass." This lesson adds the infinitive partners of the connectors in the last lesson: *a fin de* and *con el objeto de* + infinitive. One subject means an infinitive, and two subjects mean *que* + subjunctive.

sections.title: One subject or two?
rows: I work to buy a house. (I work, and I buy.)
Trabajo para que mi hijo compre una casa.
I work so that my son buys a house. (two people)
Salimos temprano a fin de llegar a tiempo.
We leave early in order to arrive on time. (one subject)
Salimos temprano a fin de que ellos lleguen a tiempo.
We leave early so that they arrive on time. (two subjects)
Viajó con el objeto de conocer el país.
She travelled in order to get to know the country.

items.spanish: El alcalde viajó a la capital con el objeto de reunirse con la ministra.
items.english: The mayor travelled to the capital in order to meet the minister.

items.spanish: Reservamos con tiempo a fin de conseguir buenos precios.
items.english: We booked in advance in order to get good prices.

items.spanish: Hizo varias gestiones a fin de obtener el permiso.
items.english: She took several steps in order to get the permit.

items.spanish: Aprendí inglés para trabajar en el extranjero.
items.english: I learned English in order to work abroad.

sections.content: English lets you add a second subject ("I work so that I can buy a house"), and learners sometimes copy it. In Spanish, say *Trabajo para comprar una casa*, not *Trabajo para que yo compre una casa*. The infinitive has no ending to change, so who acts is clear from the main verb: *a fin de llegar* is "in order to arrive" for whoever is speaking.
